id: Q9HTH9

product_type: PROTEIN

taxon:
  id: NCBITaxon:208964
  label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1
description: >-
  cdhB (PA5385) encodes the betainyl-CoA thioesterase of Pseudomonas
  aeruginosa, a hotdog-fold acyl-CoA thioesterase (PANTHER PTHR31793 subfamily
  SF2) that hydrolyzes betainyl-CoA (N,N,N-trimethylglycyl-CoA) to glycine
  betaine and free coenzyme A. This is the last step of aerobic L-carnitine
  catabolism after CdhA and CdhC, and it regenerates the CoA consumed by CdhC.
  Despite the legacy name "betainyl-CoA thiolase", the protein is a hydrolase,
  not a thiolase. cdhB is induced by carnitine through CdhR and is required for
  growth on carnitine.
existing_annotations:
- term:
    id: GO:0009437
    label: carnitine metabolic process
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000041
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - UniPathway:UPA00117
  review:
    summary: Correct but less specific than carnitine catabolic process.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: >-
      CdhB acts in the degradative route; GO:0042413 is the specific child
      and is on this gene by IMP.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0042413
      label: carnitine catabolic process
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:PSEAE/cdhB/cdhB-uniprot.txt
      record_section: ["CC:FUNCTION"]
      supporting_text: >-
        Is involved in a L-carnitine degradation pathway that allows
        P.aeruginosa to grow on L-carnitine as the sole source of carbon
        and nitrogen (PubMed:19406895).
- term:
    id: GO:0042413
    label: carnitine catabolic process
  evidence_type: IMP
  original_reference_id: PMID:19406895
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: Disruption abolishes growth on carnitine; CdhB performs the last step to glycine 
      betaine.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: >-
      CdhB catalyzes a step of carnitine breakdown (betainyl-CoA hydrolysis),
      and its disruption abolishes growth on carnitine.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:19406895
      supporting_text: >-
        The PA5388-PA5384 region contains the predicted P. aeruginosa
        carnitine dehydrogenase homologue along with other genes required for
        growth on carnitine.
    - reference_id: file:PSEAE/cdhB/cdhB-uniprot.txt
      record_section: ["CC:DISRUPTION PHENOTYPE"]
      supporting_text: "DISRUPTION PHENOTYPE: Cells are incapable of growth on carnitine."
- term:
    id: GO:0047617
    label: fatty acyl-CoA hydrolase activity
  evidence_type: IBA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000033
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - PANTHER:PTN001273712
  - UniProtKB:P77712
  - UniProtKB:Q55777
  review:
    summary: >-
      PAINT IBA from PTN001273712, seeded by E. coli FadM (SF24) and a
      Synechocystis 1,4-dihydroxy-2-naphthoyl-CoA hydrolase (SF37). CdhB is an
      acyl-CoA hydrolase, but its substrate, betainyl-CoA, is not a fatty
      acyl-CoA.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: >-
      The thioesterase chemistry is inherited and correct; the fatty-acyl
      substrate is not. GO defines fatty acyl-CoA hydrolase activity with a
      fatty acid product, whereas CdhB releases glycine betaine. The correct
      level is the parent acyl-CoA hydrolase activity ("an acyl-CoA + H2O =
      a carboxylate + CoA + H+"), which is what the measured EC 3.1.2.33
      reaction instantiates.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0016289
      label: acyl-CoA hydrolase activity
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:PSEAE/cdhB/cdhB-uniprot.txt
      record_section: ["CC:CATALYTIC ACTIVITY"]
      supporting_text: >-
        Reaction=N,N,N-trimethylglycyl-CoA + H2O = glycine betaine + CoA +
        H(+);
    - reference_id: file:interpro/panther/PTHR31793/PTHR31793-paint.tsv
      supporting_text: "PTHR31793\tPTN001273712\tGO:0047617\tF\tIBD\tfalse"
    - reference_id: file:PSEAE/cdhB/cdhB-uniprot.txt
      record_section: ["CC:FUNCTION"]
      supporting_text: >-
        Catalyzes the cleavage of betainyl-CoA (N,N,N- trimethylglycyl-CoA)
        into glycine betaine and coenzyme A (PubMed:24240508).
    - reference_id: file:PSEAE/cdhB/cdhB-uniprot.txt
      supporting_text: "EC=3.1.2.33;"
      record_section:
      - CC:CATALYTIC ACTIVITY
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: PROPAGATION_BAD
      failure_modes:
      - FUNCTIONAL_DIVERGENCE
      source_entities:
      - source_id: PANTHER:PTN001273712
        source_label: PTHR31793 node carrying fatty acyl-CoA hydrolase
        source_status: SUPPORTS_SOURCE_BUT_NOT_TARGET
        comment: >-
          The node spans SF24 (FadM), SF37 (YbgC/DHNA-CoA hydrolases) and
          SF2 (CdhB); the fatty-acyl substrate holds for FadM but not for
          the betainyl-CoA-specific SF2 branch.
      - source_id: UniProtKB:P77712
        source_label: FadM (Escherichia coli)
        source_status: SUPPORTS_SOURCE_BUT_NOT_TARGET
        comment: Long-chain acyl-CoA thioesterase; its substrate class does not transfer to CdhB.
    source_defects:
    - defect_type: WRONG_TERM
      resource: GO_CENTRAL
      slot: GO ID
      requested_change: REPOINT
      asserted_value: GO:0047617
      corrected_value: GO:0016289
      cause: OTHER
      confidence: PROBABLE
      explanation: >-
        PAINT places fatty acyl-CoA hydrolase activity at PTN001273712, a
        node that includes the betainyl-CoA thioesterase subfamily SF2; the
        fatty-acyl substrate should be restricted to the FadM branch, or the
        node term generalized to acyl-CoA hydrolase activity.
- term:
    id: GO:0016289
    label: acyl-CoA hydrolase activity
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:24240508
  qualifier: enables
  review:
    summary: >-
      Core activity: betainyl-CoA thioesterase (EC 3.1.2.33), recorded at the
      closest existing GO parent.
    action: NEW
    reason: >-
      Historical proposal retained but retired as redundant: the same molecular function is already supplied
      by the existing MODIFY replacement in this review. The biochemical activity and core function remain
      supported; retirement does not withdraw the reaction. Main-article target assays remain represented
      through curated UniProt experimental statements; accessible supplementary measurements of other
      BKACE members are not relabeled as target assays.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:PSEAE/cdhB/cdhB-uniprot.txt

      supporting_text: >-

    - reference_id: file:PSEAE/cdhB/cdhB-uniprot.txt

      record_section:
      - CC:CATALYTIC ACTIVITY

# cdhB (Q9HTH9) curation notes

## 2026-11-04 — review for the bacterial L-carnitine catabolism module

- Scaffolded with `just fetch-gene PSEAE cdhB` while generalizing
  `modules/bacterial_l_carnitine_catabolism.yaml` beyond P. putida KT2440.
- No provider deep research was generated for this gene in this session (no
  provider run was available); no `-deep-research-*.md` file exists. The review
  rests on the curated UniProt entry, GOA, and the cached publications.
- Literature checked: PMID:19406895 (Wargo and Hogan 2009, P. aeruginosa
  carnitine locus; abstract only), PMID:24240508 (Bastard et al. 2014, BKACE
  screen; abstract only), PMID:19919675 (Chen et al. 2010, Cbc/CaiX; full text),
  PMID:30670548 (Bazire et al. 2019, S. meliloti carnitine metabolism; abstract
  only, PMC6416908 full text could not be retrieved), PMID:4302217 (Aurich et al.
  1968, P. aeruginosa carnitine dehydrogenase; no abstract cached).
- Where the cached paper is abstract-only, experimental detail (kinetics,
  disruption phenotypes, EC assignment) is quoted from the UniProt statements
  that carry ECO:0000269 evidence for that paper.
- GO has no exact terms for EC 2.3.1.317 (CdhC/BcoG) or EC 3.1.2.33
  (CdhB/BcoE-BcoF C-terminal region); these are recorded as proposed_new_terms
  and annotated at the parents GO:0016747 and GO:0016289.


## 2026-11-07 — independent PAO1 consultation

CdhB hydrolyzes betainyl-CoA after CdhC-dependent CoA transfer. The broad fatty-acyl-CoA hydrolase mapping is refined to the existing acyl-CoA hydrolase replacement. Original fourth row (zero-based index 3) proposes exactly the same GO:0016289 as the third row (zero-based index 2) already supplies by MODIFY. This author-created duplicate proposal is retained with its original NEW action and payload, marked retired at annotation level, and all of its distinct support is copied into the active replacement and core. No activity or evidence is withdrawn.

Source scope and access receipts are preserved in [primary-scope](../../../analysis/module_audits/bacterial_l_carnitine_catabolism/pseae-consultation/primary-scope.md). The genuine Falcon attempt failed with HTTP 403 authentication/access rejection; no provider report was invented. The original ordered source payloads and protected caches remain intact. The mapped PANTHER lineage has no reported IRD/IKR loss. All primary source quotations are distinguished from analyst interpretation.

        <p>cdhB (PA5385) encodes the betainyl-CoA thioesterase of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a hotdog-fold acyl-CoA thioesterase (PANTHER PTHR31793 subfamily SF2) that hydrolyzes betainyl-CoA (N,N,N-trimethylglycyl-CoA) to glycine betaine and free coenzyme A. This is the last step of aerobic L-carnitine catabolism after CdhA and CdhC, and it regenerates the CoA consumed by CdhC. Despite the legacy name "betainyl-CoA thiolase", the protein is a hydrolase, not a thiolase. cdhB is induced by carnitine through CdhR and is required for growth on carnitine.</p>

                <h1 id="pp_0301-q88r33-in-pseudomonas-putida-kt2440-a-cytoplasmic-betainyl-coa-thioesterase-of-the-l-carnitine-catabolic-pathway">PP_0301 (Q88R33) in <em>Pseudomonas putida</em> KT2440: A Cytoplasmic Betainyl-CoA Thioesterase of the L-Carnitine Catabolic Pathway</h1>
<h2 id="summary">Summary</h2>
<p>The gene <strong>PP_0301</strong> (UniProt <strong>Q88R33</strong>; OrderedLocusNames PP_0301) of <em>Pseudomonas putida</em> KT2440 encodes a small (156-residue), single-domain, <strong>HotDog-fold acyl-CoA thioesterase</strong> belonging to the 4-hydroxybenzoyl-CoA thioesterase (4HBT) family. Its physiological function is that of a <strong>betainyl-CoA thioesterase</strong> (gene name <strong>cdhB</strong>; EC <strong>3.1.2.33</strong>; KEGG ortholog <strong>K27492</strong>), catalyzing the hydrolysis of the CoA thioester of glycine betaine:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>betainyl-CoA + H₂O → glycine betaine + CoA</strong></p>
</blockquote>
<p>This reaction is the third, CoA-releasing step of the <strong>L-carnitine catabolic pathway</strong> encoded by the compact, co-oriented operon <strong>PP_0301–PP_0305</strong>. Within this pathway, L-carnitine is first oxidized to 3-dehydrocarnitine by carnitine 3-dehydrogenase (lcdH/cdhA, PP_0302, EC 1.1.1.108), the 3-dehydrocarnitine is then cleaved by the β-keto-acid cleavage enzyme cdhC (PP_0303, EC 2.3.1.317) to yield <strong>betainyl-CoA</strong> (with concomitant acetoacetate formation from acetyl-CoA), and finally PP_0301/cdhB hydrolyzes betainyl-CoA to release <strong>glycine betaine</strong> and free CoA. Glycine betaine is a central branch-point metabolite that is subsequently funneled into the conserved, cytoplasmic glycine-betaine demethylation pathway (GB → dimethylglycine → sarcosine → glycine), enabling the bacterium to use L-carnitine as a source of carbon and nitrogen.</p>
<p>A key outcome of this investigation is an <strong>annotation correction</strong>. The legacy name carried in the genome submission — "betainyl-CoA thiolase" with EC 2.3.1.- (an acyltransferase/thiolase class) — is a <strong>misannotation</strong>. Every domain and family assignment for Q88R33 is unanimous for a HotDog-fold thioester <strong>hydrolase</strong> (EC class 3.1.2.-), and the protein's small size (~156 aa, a single HotDog domain) is inconsistent with genuine thiolases (~400 aa, two-domain acyltransferases). The correct designation is a <strong>betainyl-CoA thioesterase (hydrolase)</strong>. This functional assignment is strongly supported by 1:1 orthology to the experimentally validated <em>Pseudomonas aeruginosa</em> gene PA5385 (cdhB), which resides in a transposon-screen-confirmed carnitine-catabolism locus.</p>
<p>The protein is a soluble, <strong>cytoplasmic</strong> enzyme — it has no signal peptide or transmembrane segments (confirmed by a hydropathy scan), and its CoA-thioester substrate is strictly intracellular. Its L-carnitine substrate enters the cell through the co-encoded ABC transporter (substrate-binding protein PP_0304). An experimental crystal structure of the <em>P. putida</em> protein itself exists (PDB 2HLJ, 2.00 Å), confirming the HotDog thioesterase fold.</p>
<hr />
<h2 id="key-findings">Key Findings</h2>
<h3 id="f001-pp_0301-is-a-hotdog-fold-thioesterase-not-a-thiolase-annotation-corrected">F001 — PP_0301 is a HotDog-fold thioesterase, not a thiolase (annotation corrected)</h3>
<p>UniProt Q88R33 is a small <strong>156-amino-acid single-domain protein</strong>. The domain and family assignments across all major resources converge unanimously on a <strong>HotDog-fold acyl-CoA thioesterase</strong>:</p>

<p>Critically, an <strong>experimental crystal structure exists</strong>: <strong>PDB 2HLJ</strong>, an X-ray structure at 2.00 Å resolution (chains A = residues 1–156), solved by the Joint Center for Structural Genomics (JCSG/PSI-2) and titled <em>"Crystal structure of a putative thioesterase from Pseudomonas putida KT2440."</em> This directly confirms the HotDog thioesterase fold experimentally for the exact protein in question.</p>
<p>The legacy genome-submission name "betainyl-CoA <strong>thiolase</strong>" (EC 2.3.1.-) is therefore a <strong>misnomer</strong>. Thiolases and other EC 2.3.1.- acyltransferases <em>transfer</em> an acyl group and are typically ~400-residue, two-domain enzymes. PP_0301 is instead a <strong>hydrolase</strong> (EC 3.1.2.-): it cleaves a thioester bond with water, releasing a free acid and CoA. Its small single-domain architecture is diagnostic of the HotDog thioesterase superfamily rather than the thiolase superfamily.</p>
<p>The mechanistic identity of the family is well established in the literature. HotDog-fold thioesterases catalyze hydrolysis of thioester bonds of acyl-CoA substrates (<a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26067557/">PMID: 26067557</a>: <em>"It belongs to the hotdog-fold thioesterase superfamily and catalyzes hydrolysis of thioester bonds of acyl-CoA in vitro, while its in vivo function remains unrevealed."</em>). Acyl-CoA thioesterases more broadly <em>"catalyze the hydrolysis of fatty acyl-CoA to free fatty acid and CoA and thereby regulate lipid metabolism and cellular signaling"</em> (<a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17563367/">PMID: 17563367</a>), and the structural determinants for substrate recognition and catalysis by these enzymes have been dissected in the <em>E. coli</em> paralogs YbdB and YdiI (<a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25010423/">PMID: 25010423</a>: <em>"the structural determinants for substrate recognition and catalysis in two hotdog-fold thioesterase paralogs, YbdB and YdiI from Escherichia coli, are identified and analyzed"</em>).</p>
<h3 id="f002-pp_0301-cdhb-betainyl-coa-thioesterase-ec-31233">F002 — PP_0301 = cdhB, betainyl-CoA thioesterase (EC 3.1.2.33)</h3>
<p>KEGG assigns <strong>ppu:PP_0301</strong> to ortholog <strong>K27492 = cdhB = "betainyl-CoA thioesterase [EC:3.1.2.33]."</strong> The EC 3.1.2.33 entry (reaction RN R13307) defines the catalyzed reaction as:</p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>betainyl-CoA + H₂O = glycine betaine + CoA</strong> (systematic name: <em>betaine-CoA hydrolase</em>)</p>
</blockquote>
<p>The KEGG comment notes that <em>"the enzyme, characterized from the bacterium Pseudomonas aeruginosa, is involved in an L-carnitine degradation pathway."</em> The <strong>substrate specificity</strong> is the CoA thioester of glycine betaine (betainyl-CoA); the enzyme hydrolyzes this thioester to release free glycine betaine plus CoA. This assignment is fully consistent with (i) the HotDog 4HBT fold — a small, single-domain thioesterase scaffold — and (ii) the substrate implied by the protein's own legacy name ("betainyl-CoA"). The reaction it catalyzes matches the general acyl-CoA thioesterase chemistry of the family (hydrolysis of an acyl-CoA to free acid + CoA), specialized here for the quaternary-ammonium acyl group of glycine betaine.</p>

<h3 id="f004-cytoplasmic-localization-product-feeds-the-gbdr-regulated-demethylation-pathway">F004 — Cytoplasmic localization; product feeds the GbdR-regulated demethylation pathway</h3>
<p>PP_0301 is a <strong>soluble, single-domain cytoplasmic enzyme</strong>. It carries no signal peptide and no transmembrane segments (confirmed by a hydropathy scan), and its CoA-thioester substrate is strictly intracellular (CoA thioesters do not cross membranes). The upstream substrate, L-carnitine, is imported via the co-encoded ABC transporter (substrate-binding protein PP_0304). Thus the enzyme performs its chemistry in the <strong>cytoplasm</strong>.</p>
<p>Its product, <strong>glycine betaine (GB)</strong>, is the branch-point metabolite of quaternary-amine catabolism in pseudomonads. In the closely related <em>P. aeruginosa</em>, GB is degraded in the cytoplasm by a multistep demethylation route (GB → dimethylglycine → sarcosine → glycine), which lets the bacterium use GB — and its precursors choline and carnitine — as sole sources of carbon and nitrogen (<a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23354714/">PMID: 23354714</a>: <em>"a variety of soil- and water-dwelling bacteria have catabolic pathways for the multistep conversion of choline, via GB, to glycine and can thereby use choline and GB as sole sources of carbon and nitrogen"</em>). This catabolic locus is controlled by the AraC-family regulator <strong>GbdR</strong>, whose regulon <em>"includes the genes encoding GB, dimethylglycine, sarcosine, glycine, and serine catabolic enzymes and the BetX and CbcXWV quaternary amine transport proteins"</em> (<a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24097953/">PMID: 24097953</a>). This mirrors the CdhR/AraC regulator (PP_0305) that governs the carnitine branch in <em>P. putida</em>.</p>
<h3 id="f005-primary-literature-confirms-the-carnitine-3-dehydrocarnitine-glycine-betaine-route">F005 — Primary literature confirms the carnitine → 3-dehydrocarnitine → glycine betaine route</h3>
<p>The two enzymatic steps flanking and including PP_0301 are anchored in primary experimental literature:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Wargo & Hogan 2009</strong> (<a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19406895/">PMID: 19406895</a>) performed a transposon-mutant genetic screen in <em>P. aeruginosa</em> PA14 that experimentally established the carnitine catabolic route: <em>"carnitine is converted to 3-dehydrocarnitine (3-dhc) which is in turn metabolized to glycine betaine (GB), an intermediate metabolite in the catabolism of carnitine to glycine."</em> They also <em>"confirmed that an intact GB catabolic pathway is required for growth on carnitine,"</em> showing that carnitine catabolism funnels through glycine betaine — the very product of PP_0301.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Bastard et al. 2014</strong> (<a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24240508/">PMID: 24240508</a>) defined the <strong>DUF849 / β-keto acid cleavage enzyme (BKACE)</strong> family that provides the EC 2.3.1.317 activity (cdhC): <em>"we investigated the DUF849 Pfam family and unearthed 14 potential new enzymatic activities, leading to the designation of these proteins as β-keto acid cleavage enzymes."</em> This is the enzyme that generates the <strong>betainyl-CoA substrate</strong> hydrolyzed by PP_0301.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Wargo, Szwergold & Hogan 2008</strong> (<a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17951379/">PMID: 17951379</a>) biochemically defined the downstream glycine-betaine demethylation genes and the AraC regulator GbdR in <em>P. aeruginosa</em>: <em>"Glycine betaine (GB), which occurs freely in the environment and is an intermediate in the catabolism of choline and carnitine, can serve as a sole source of carbon or nitrogen in Pseudomonas aeruginosa."</em></p>
</li>
</ul>
<p>The KT2440 cluster PP_0301–PP_0305 (cdhB, lcdH/cdhA, cdhC, transporter, cdhR) is the direct ortholog of the <em>P. aeruginosa</em> carnitine-catabolism locus.</p>

<p><strong>Why the "thiolase" name is wrong and the "thioesterase" assignment is right.</strong> The genome-submission label reflects an early, sequence-blind guess. Three independent lines of evidence overturn it:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Fold / size</strong> — Q88R33 is a 156-aa single HotDog domain (confirmed experimentally by PDB 2HLJ), not a ~400-aa two-domain thiolase. Every domain database (InterPro, Pfam, CDD, Gene3D, SUPFAM, PANTHER, eggNOG) classifies it as a 4HBT HotDog thioesterase.</li>
<li><strong>Chemistry</strong> — HotDog 4HBT enzymes <em>hydrolyze</em> acyl-CoA thioesters (EC 3.1.2.-), releasing free acid + CoA; thiolases (EC 2.3.1.-) instead <em>transfer</em> acyl groups. The KEGG-assigned EC 3.1.2.33 reaction (betainyl-CoA + H₂O → glycine betaine + CoA) is a hydrolysis.</li>
<li><strong>Pathway logic and orthology</strong> — The enzyme sits immediately downstream of a BKACE that <em>produces</em> betainyl-CoA, and it is 1:1 orthologous to the experimentally validated <em>P. aeruginosa</em> cdhB (PA5385). A thioesterase that liberates glycine betaine + CoA is exactly what the pathway requires at this position; a thiolase would not fit.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Biological role.</strong> By hydrolyzing betainyl-CoA, PP_0301 (i) liberates glycine betaine for entry into the demethylation pathway, and (ii) regenerates free CoA, which is essential for continued flux through the acetyl-CoA-dependent cdhC step. The enzyme thereby couples carnitine breakdown to the universal quaternary-amine catabolic hub (glycine betaine → glycine), allowing <em>P. putida</em> to exploit carnitine as a carbon and nitrogen source in the soil and rhizosphere environments where carnitine and its relatives are common.</p>

<h2 id="limitations-and-knowledge-gaps">Limitations and Knowledge Gaps</h2>
<ol>
<li><strong>No direct biochemical assay of PP_0301 itself.</strong> The EC 3.1.2.33 activity was characterized in the <em>P. aeruginosa</em> enzyme; the <em>P. putida</em> ortholog's activity and kinetic parameters (kcat, Km for betainyl-CoA) are inferred, not measured. The PDB 2HLJ structure was deposited as a "putative thioesterase" without a bound substrate or functional assay.</li>
<li><strong>Substrate specificity breadth is unquantified.</strong> HotDog thioesterases can be promiscuous. Whether PP_0301 is strictly specific for betainyl-CoA or also hydrolyzes other short-chain or quaternary-amine acyl-CoAs is unknown.</li>
<li><strong>Regulation in <em>P. putida</em> is inferred from <em>P. aeruginosa</em>.</strong> The role of PP_0305 (CdhR) and PP_0298 (a glycine-betaine-responsive AraC regulator) in inducing PP_0301 in KT2440 is predicted by orthology and operon context, not directly demonstrated.</li>
<li><strong>Phenotype not directly tested in KT2440.</strong> A PP_0301 deletion has not been reported; its necessity for growth of <em>P. putida</em> on carnitine is inferred from the <em>P. aeruginosa</em> transposon screen.</li>
<li><strong>Legacy annotation persistence.</strong> Public databases still carry the "betainyl-CoA thiolase / EC 2.3.1.-" label; downstream tools relying on this may propagate the misannotation.</li>
</ol>

<li><strong>Genetic knockout / complementation.</strong> Construct a ΔPP_0301 mutant in <em>P. putida</em> KT2440 and test growth on L-carnitine and glycine betaine as sole C/N sources; complement to confirm the phenotype maps to PP_0301. <h2 id="conclusion">Conclusion</h2>
<p>PP_0301 (Q88R33) is a cytoplasmic, single-domain HotDog-fold (4HBT) acyl-CoA thioesterase functioning as a <strong>betainyl-CoA thioesterase (cdhB; EC 3.1.2.33)</strong>. The genome-legacy name "betainyl-CoA thiolase" (EC 2.3.1.-) is a misannotation; the enzyme is a thioester hydrolase, not a thiolase.</p>
